title: four months of rain
hookLine: a new king goes to his palace, and the man who made him king goes to a cave
carry: chaturmas, the four holy months of rain

lines: TWO BROTHERS WALK TO THE HILLS.
cards: Sugriva is crowned. Angada is named heir. The city celebrates with drums and garlands.

And Rama doesn't go in. He's an exile, he says, and he promised fourteen years outside any village or town. So the new king of Kishkindha goes to his palace, and the man who made him king walks off to live in a cave.
Valmiki doesn't rush past it: the city lit up, and two brothers walking away from it into the hills.

teach.b: It's the start of the rainy season. Rama explains: you can't send search parties across the land in the monsoon. Rivers flood, roads vanish.
Enjoy your kingdom for these months, he tells Sugriva; when autumn comes, we search.

So Rama and Lakshmana go to a mountain called Prasravana and find a wide cave to wait out the rain. Four months, and nothing to do but wait, for a man whose wife is a prisoner somewhere he can't even name.
Lakshmana makes it bearable. When Rama sinks into grief, Lakshmana reminds him who he is, and to save his strength for the time to act.
And Valmiki fills the chapter with what they see: peaks, rushing water, flowering trees, birds. Hindus still keep these months.

They're called chaturmas, the four months. Many traditions say Vishnu goes into his deep sleep on Devshayani Ekadashi, early in the rains, and wakes on Prabodhini Ekadashi in the autumn month of Kartik.
Through that season many monks stop wandering and stay in one place, and many households take on a vow: giving up a food, reading a scripture, adding a prayer.

Some teachers read Rama's cave as that season in story form: when you can't move, you keep your vow and gather strength. Now the week, by its teachings: dasya, love that serves. Sakhya, friendship sworn before the fire.
Touching an elder's feet. A promise given once is kept. Dharma is subtle.

teach.h: THE WEEK, AND THE RAIN COMING IN.
teach.b: And today, chaturmas, and the rain coming in.

how: The four months of the rainy season, chaturmasa, are still kept by some Hindu ascetics and households as a time to stay in one place, travel less, and take on extra vows and study.

o: a flood that sweeps away Sugriva's palace
a storm Ravana sends to stop the search
the monsoon months Rama waits out in a cave

games.q: the crowning and the cave — tap the pairs.
p: the four holy months of rain

s: Rama moves into the palace at Kishkindha
he keeps his exile vow and stays outside, in a mountain cave.
the search waits for the end of the rains
rivers flood and roads vanish; autumn is the time to set out.
chaturmas is an old custom nobody keeps anymore
many monks and households still keep vows through these months.

games.q: your grandmother says she's giving up a food until the rains end. by today's lesson, what's going on?
o: a chaturmas vow, kept through the four holy months.
a doctor's diet she's embarrassed about.
a punishment for something she did.
games.why: in chaturmas many Hindus take on a vow for the rainy months, the season Rama waited out in the cave on Prasravana.

practice: Listen. If there's rain, listen to it; if not, to whatever's there: traffic, a fan, your own breath. Let the sound be the whole practice.
If you pray, choose one small vow for this season, the way families do for chaturmas: one food, one page, one prayer. If you don't, choose one small steady habit to keep while you wait for something.

wordCard.voice: The rains. Sugriva is crowned, and Rama waits out the monsoon in a cave on Prasravana mountain.

orig.note: Sanskrit varṣā: the rains, the monsoon season. related to varṣa, rain, and also year.

carryVoice: Your line: chaturmas, the four holy months of rain. Rama keeps his vow in a cave and waits for autumn. Day five hundred eighty-eight, done.
